198.text: All right, have it your way. Heroically, you throw yourself onto your sword. Nothing happens! No blood, no pain, absolutely nothing! Frustrated, you try again. Still nothing. If only your girlfriend could see you now. You don't make an exit this stylish every day! Then it is over, and everything goes dark... Some time later, you wake to find yourself floating in a dark space. You shudder. Is this the afterlife? Is this really all there is? Not a bright prospect... Then you realise what woke you. A gentle voice drifts towards you, faint and distant. "Dave Parker!" it whispers. "You should know that no one can escape their destiny. Fleeing it is pointless: fate always catches up with you! Go and complete the tasks you have been given. By my divine authority, I grant you an extra life, and one more chance to fulfil your destiny..." As the voice fades, everything starts spinning. You grow dizzy and fall into a deep, dreamless sleep. When you open your eyes again, you are exactly where you tried to kill yourself...

209.text: Your hotel room is small, but quite cosy for the price. Against the west wall stands a wardrobe decorated with elaborate folk-art paintings. Then you snap out of your reverie: weren't you supposed to call home when you arrived? Oh well. With so much to take in, surely Mum can wait a little longer.

210.text: This is the lobby of "Mary's Inn", your home for the next few weeks. A door in the east wall opens onto the street; an opening to the north leads to reception. The place is deserted, and the emptiness is rather depressing. Still, perhaps things will pick up at breakfast tomorrow. Looking around, you get the impression the decorators were desperate to show how prosperous and worldly their little village is. Sadly, they tried rather too hard. The result reminds you of the hotel lobbies in American soap operas, with one tiny difference: those are about five times bigger! Never mind. At least the scenery is fantastic, and that's what you came for, isn't it?

On the other hand, the mountain lake is just a little farther north, and you did want to cool those steaming feet. If a drink at the hotel bar sounds more tempting, you can follow the road back west.

215.text: As you drift south, the current grows stronger and stronger. Suddenly you realise the danger! You swim desperately against the pull, but it's too late. A vast whirlpool drags you, thrashing, to the bottom of the mountain lake, where you drown in agony... In your final moments, you think you glimpse the golden domes of the sunken city the locals told you about. Unfortunately, given your present circumstances, you are unlikely to get the chance to confirm their story. You don't even have time for one last prayer...

216.text: You stand on the shore of Loch Calderwood, speechless at the view. Before you lies a picturesque mountain lake, ringed by high, jagged peaks behind which the sun is slowly setting. To the northwest, a waterfall roars down from the mountains. A dangerously romantic feeling comes over you, and you consider calling your girlfriend. Then you dismiss the idea. What chance would a soppy romantic have with the girls around here? Besides, you left your girlfriend at home for a reason, didn't you? A few lengths of the lake might be just the thing to get you in shape before you bestow your attentions on the ladies of Scotland. If you'd like a little exercise before your campaign of conquest, enter the lake to the north. Otherwise, the road south leads back to your hotel.

Candles in expensive holders on every table almost give it a first-class air. But why bother? Most of the diners are locals! One of them, an elderly man with a long beard, sits at a corner table studying the menu and savouring his beer. If you're hungry or thirsty, you could join him. Otherwise, you can leave through the door behind you.

218.text: As you wade west across the muddy lake bed, the water gets colder and deeper. Until now you could just about stand, but you're running out of bottom. Time to swim, unless you fancy sinking! "Oh well, it'll toughen me up!" you tell yourself. You splash a little water onto your heroic chest, then fling yourself forwards with magnificent disregard for your own survival. Brrr! For a summer evening, that water is cold! After a few seconds you get used to it. Quite pleasant, really. All that's missing is your rubber duck. As you make your first clumsy strokes, you feel a strong current pulling you south, towards a gigantic whirlpool that swallows anything careless enough to stray within reach. You can swim in any direction except west.

If you've sensibly changed your mind about playing the hero, head south to the shore. Or ignore my advice and continue west. You'll find out soon enough! Just remember: this was YOUR idea...

221.text: Still dazed by the waterfall's battering, you struggle to keep afloat. Then you freeze in astonishment, promptly sink and swallow a mouthful of water! When you surface, the shock hits you: you're still on the south side of the waterfall! That alone might have a perfectly reasonable explanation. You did lose your bearings underwater. You could accept it if... if... if the village were still there! But it has vanished. Where the little settlement stood, a deep, dark forest now crowds the shore, full of trees you've never seen before. Could the waterfall have brought you into a parallel world, like those daft adventures you play on your computer at home? Except THIS is real! Where the hell have you ended up?

It doesn't take much imagination to work out that this is likely to be your last solo holiday until you're legally an adult...

The graceful creature cannot withstand those long, sharp teeth much longer...

You probably don't get German newspapers here anyway, do you?" The girl, equally red-faced, hurriedly says no. Ignoring the good ten years between you, you reassure her in a fatherly tone: "Never mind, my child. I can't speak German anyway!" You roar with laughter. The local, who has been minding his own business, rolls his eyes as though your joke has caught him squarely between the legs. Discovering that the waitress also suffers from a chronic lack of humour, you cut your performance short and dismiss her with a gracious wave. Once she has disappeared into the kitchen, you ask the old man about the village and its surroundings. He slowly mumbles into his beard that he knows an interesting legend. Fine. You weren't expecting a list of trendy nightspots and yuppie discos, but does it have to be a fairy tale? You prop your head on your hands, just in case you nod off and hit your nose on the table. Longing for your food so you'll at least have something to do, you listen. Long ago, a rich, proud city stood where Loch Calderwood lies today. In a single night it vanished, leaving a lake at the foot of the mountains! People said the gods had punished its inhabitants for their pride and vanity. They were said to be wealthy and wonderfully skilled craftsmen. You've been practising the art of sleeping with your eyes open, but the old man mistakes your stare for amazement and goes one better. Even now, the villagers claim you can see the city's towers and rooftops if you dive to the bottom of the lake at midnight under a full moon. A very exclusive, once-in-a-lifetime experience, apparently. Not one of the brave men who tried it ever came back...
